findings:
🟠 [prepush-existing-ref-range] MUST-FIX `.githooks/lib/test-identity-gate.sh` `test_identity_refuse_push_range`: for an existing remote ref the commit set is `remote_sha..local_sha`, which excludes only that ref's old tip, not history already on the remote. With the 632 Test User commits on origin/develop (§0), updating any other existing origin branch that picks up develop history (a release/main fast-forward, a feature branch that merged develop) is refused, contradicting the P3 NC "a push whose only test-identity commits are already on the target remote passes"; the only way out is `--no-verify`, which also skips the QC gate. This is G8's literal two-dot formula, so the defect is against the NC and G8's stated purpose ("only history already on THAT remote is excluded"). Same branch, force-push: when `remote_sha` is not in the local object DB, `rev-list` fails, `2>/dev/null || true` yields an empty set and the push passes unchecked. New branch, deleted ref (all-zero local sha skipped) and force-push over a known tip are correct. Fix: use `git rev-list "$local_sha" --not --remotes="$remote"` for both cases, adding `"$remote_sha"` to the exclusions only when `git cat-file -e "$remote_sha^{commit}"` succeeds; add one fixture case each.
🟠 [outer-exit-no-group-term] MUST-FIX `hooks/tests/run.sh`: G5 requires "TERM the child's process group, wait until the group is gone" on EXIT as well as INT/TERM, but only `__ts_outer_on_interrupt` signals the group; `__suite_on_exit` goes straight to `ts_guard_after` and `ts_snapshot_remove`. Because the inner run is in its own session: (a) on a normal child exit, surviving descendants keep running while `$SNAP` is removed under them; (b) when the outer dies by any other signal (HUP on terminal or ssh close), bash still runs the EXIT trap, so the snapshot is deleted while the whole inner suite carries on detached, whereas before this diff the terminal's HUP reached the suite; (c) a descendant that recreates a path under `$SNAP` leaves a container with no lock file, which the reaper skips forever; (d) an INT landing while `__suite_on_exit` is inside `rm -rf` re-enters the handler and exits mid-removal. Fix: at the top of `__suite_on_exit`, when a child was started, `trap '' INT TERM`, TERM the child's group/session, call `ts_wait_pgid_gone`, and only then run the guard and removal.
🟡 [child-pid-race] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `hooks/tests/run.sh` trap/child-start races (the INT/TERM traps themselves are installed before any snapshot resource exists): (i) a signal between `( … ) &` and `TS_CHILD_PID=$!` runs the handler with an empty pid, so the outer exits and removes the snapshot under a live inner; (ii) an INT before the subshell reaches `trap - INT`/`setsid` is ignored by the async subshell, `ts_wait_pgid_gone` sees no group yet, and the outer then blocks in `wait` with INT/TERM ignored for the whole suite. Remediation: fall back to `jobs -p` when `TS_CHILD_PID` is empty and re-signal until `wait` reaps. Excluded because both windows are a few milliseconds wide after a ~3 s construction; (i) closes for free if the EXIT-path fix above uses the `jobs -p` fallback.
🟡 [pgid-int-flake] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `P4 pgid: … expected 130, got 0`: I judge this test timing, not the outer signal handling, with moderate confidence. In that case INT goes only to the inner group; the outer is never signalled and returns the inner's wait status verbatim (`wait; TS_CHILD_STATUS=$?; exit`), so no outer trap path can turn 130 into 0. A 0 means the inner run finished normally, i.e. the INT was not acted on inside it; the inner sequential runner is not in this diff, so I could not pin that side. The test's readiness loop falls through after 10 s without asserting the marker, so under load it can send INT before the fixture test is in `sleep`. Remediation: fail when the marker is absent and widen the budget. Excluded because 6 of 6 solo runs are green and the outer contract is not implicated.
